qt: to the Commission Marion Maréchal (ECR) Subject:
Non-compliance with technological neutrality by the 2023 EU Energy Efficiency Directive – revision of Article 15

Directive (EU)2023/1791 of 13 September 2023 on energy efficiency requires, as far as possible, the individualisation of heating costs. Where the installation of an individual meter is uneconomical or technically impossible, it provides, inter alia, that ‘individual heat cost allocators shall be used to measure heat consumption at each radiator’1. This provision, which is the result of a regulatory framework that is increasingly out of step with technological progress, is unfair to companies that, while offering innovative measurement solutions that meet the requirements of reliability, accuracy and consumer protection, do not measure heat consumption ‘at each radiator’. In fact, this latter provision unduly hinders the development of technologies based on indoor temperature sensors and algorithms (‘digital twin of the building’), even though they are certified by the legal metrology authorities as heating cost allocators. 1.

While Article 18 provides an incentive to stimulate competition in sub-metering services, does the Commission plan, in the context of the evaluation of the Directive due by 28 February 2027, to review and amend Article 15 in order to comply with the principle of technological neutrality?
If not, how does it justify maintaining a provision that is manifestly contrary to competition law?
Article 15 of Directive (EU)2023/1791 of 13 September 2023 on energy efficiency.
